contract: F-24, the engine install marker `.hilbertraum-runtime.json` and the copy beside it (plan Appendix B; W-84; docs/app-updates.md §6.7, §6.11): which files of an engine copy release 1's pre-spawn check reads, and what it makes of each. An addition beside vectors.json, which stays as T2.10 locked it.
reader: verifyBinaryBeforeSpawn (src/main/services/binary-verifier.ts), enforced as in a packaged build, for `program` in the copy's own folder, as the engines call it (no `startsOnMissingOther`). The marker is `fields` plus the vector's `binaries`, written into that folder by the test.
layout: `files`: the copy's files, key (`/` separators, relative to the copy's folder) to text, written as UTF-8. `binaries`: the marker's map, key to SHA-256. `longKeys` (optional): keys too long to write out, each `repeat` repeated `times` times and then `then`, with its SHA-256, added to the map. `selfLinks` (optional): keys at which the test puts a link to itself instead of a file (a junction on Windows, a symbolic link elsewhere). `sha256`: the SHA-256 of every text a map records as its true hash; any other hash in a map is wrong on purpose.
notCovered: A read error of the medium (EIO) counts like a file that is not there, by what the file is (`missing` for the program or a library, `missing-other` for any other file); no portable file system path fails with it, so binary-verifier.test.ts proves it with an injected error code, beside the holds (`unreadable`), and T11.3a's real-media row says which code a bad sector gives on each system.

vectors.name: an unrecorded file whose bytes changed

files.ggml.dll: ggml bytes, changed after the install

vectors.why: a map that records the program alone (a marker written before #998) checks the program alone: release 1 never looks at a file its marker does not record, whatever its bytes (R1 M-3)

vectors.name: an unrecorded extra file

files.ggml-cuda.dll: a backend a later release adds

vectors.why: a file in the folder that the marker does not record is never looked at and never a refusal; an unrecorded library is the recorded residual (#1025), and every later writer records every file it installs (F-24's duty) (R1 M-3)

vectors.name: a recorded file in a subfolder whose bytes changed

files.backends/ggml-vulkan.dll: vulkan bytes, changed after the install

vectors.why: every key the copy's own marker records is checked, a key in a subfolder too (a later release that lays its copy out in folders): the file differs from its record (R1 M-3)

vectors.name: keys under cpu/, cpu.new/ and cpu.old/ in a main marker, each with a wrong hash
vectors.why: the three folders hold another copy (the chat engine's safety net and its swap, #986), judged by that copy's own marker: a main marker's keys under them are set aside, for every family (no writer writes one: F-24's duty) (R1 M-3)

vectors.name: a main marker that records only files under cpu/, cpu.new/ and cpu.old/
vectors.why: in the program's own folder, a map that records files but no file of this copy (a net's own marker written with keys relative to the family, say) is damaged, never the hash-less marker of a drive older than the map; only an absent or empty map is that (vectors.json, #234: tolerated) (R1 m-2)

vectors.name: a recorded name with a NUL in it
vectors.why: the OS refuses the name itself (Node: ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE, on every system), so no file can ever be there: the record is damaged, with the reinstall offer; it was `unreadable`, "try again in a minute", on every attempt (R2 m-1)

vectors.name: a recorded name longer than any system's path limit
vectors.why: a path of 40,000 characters is ENAMETOOLONG on Windows (over 32,767), Linux (4,096) and macOS (1,024): the record names no file this copy can hold (R2 m-1)

vectors.name: a recorded file that is a link to itself
vectors.why: a link loop at a recorded path is ELOOP and never heals by waiting: refused as damaged with the reinstall offer, not `unreadable` (R1 M-4)
